"""Fixed parity inputs shared by ``make_reference.py`` (HF side) and ``parity.py`` (Axon side).

Inputs are natural text, so top-1 comparisons are not decided by near-ties on random ids.
Encoder inputs mask about 15% of the body tokens, as in MLM; decoder inputs start with the
BOS id the decoder tokenizer config asks for.
"""

import numpy as np

SENTENCES = (
    "The river bends twice before it reaches the old stone bridge at the edge of town.",
    "Most of the houses on the hill were built from timber cut in the northern forests.",
    "A small library opened in the square last spring and now lends books to every school nearby.",
    "Scientists measured the temperature of the lake every morning for three straight years.",
    "The committee voted to repair the harbor walls before the winter storms arrived.",
    "Her grandfather kept a notebook of every bird he saw from the kitchen window.",
    "Trains leave the central station every twenty minutes during the busiest hours of the day.",
    "The museum keeps maps drawn by sailors who crossed the ocean more than four centuries ago.",
    "Farmers in the valley grow wheat, barley and apples on land that floods each spring.",
    "A careful reader will notice that the second chapter quietly changes the narrator.",
    "The new bridge uses steel cables anchored deep in the rock on both sides of the gorge.",
    "During the festival, musicians play in the streets until long after midnight.",
    "The recipe calls for flour, butter, two eggs and a pinch of salt.",
    "Engineers tested the engine for several weeks before the first long flight.",
    "Children in the village learn to swim in the shallow bay behind the church.",
    "The painting shows a quiet harbor at dawn, with fishing boats returning to shore.",
    "Economists argue that the price of bread depends on the weather as much as on the market.",
    "The old lighthouse was replaced by an automatic beacon in the middle of the last century.",
    "Every Sunday the market sells cheese, honey and vegetables from the surrounding farms.",
    "The mathematician proved that the sequence grows without bound, but only very slowly.",
    "A narrow path climbs from the monastery to a lake that stays frozen until June.",
    "The city of Paris is the capital of France and sits on the river Seine.",
    "Volunteers planted more than a thousand trees along the new highway last autumn.",
    "The orchestra rehearsed the symphony for a month before the opening night.",
)
LENGTHS = {"short": 8, "medium": 300, "long": 2048}
PADDED_LENGTHS = (300, 233, 64, 9)
GENERATE_PROMPTS = (
    "The capital of France is",
    "Once upon a time, in a small village by the sea,",
    "The theory of relativity states that",
)
GENERATE_NEW_TOKENS = 64


def body_ids(tokenizer, count, seed):
    """``count`` text token ids (no special tokens) from a seeded shuffle of the sentences."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    ids = []
    while len(ids) < count:
        sentence = SENTENCES[int(rng.integers(len(SENTENCES)))]
        ids.extend(tokenizer.backend.encode(" " + sentence, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
    return ids[:count]


def sequence(tokenizer, arch, length, seed):
    """One input of exactly ``length`` ids, framed the way the checkpoint's tokenizer frames text."""
    if arch == "encoder":
        body = body_ids(tokenizer, length - 2, seed)
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1000)
        masked = rng.random(len(body)) < 0.15
        body = [tokenizer.mask_token_id if m else t for t, m in zip(body, masked)]
        return [tokenizer.bos_token_id, *body, tokenizer.eos_token_id]
    return [tokenizer.bos_token_id, *body_ids(tokenizer, length - 1, seed)]


def parity_inputs(tokenizer, arch):
    """``{case: (input_ids [B, S] int32, attention_mask [B, S] int32)}``."""
    cases = {}
    for n, (name, length) in enumerate(LENGTHS.items()):
        ids, mask = tokenizer.pad([sequence(tokenizer, arch, length, seed=n)])
        cases[name] = (ids, mask)
    rows = [sequence(tokenizer, arch, length, seed=10 + n) for n, length in enumerate(PADDED_LENGTHS)]
    cases["padded"] = tokenizer.pad(rows)
    return cases

"""HF transformers reference outputs (FP32, CPU, eager attention) for the parity tests.

Tool code: imports torch and transformers; never imported by the runtime.

    python -m scripts.ettin_axon.make_reference --model ettin-encoder-17m ettin-decoder-17m
writes ``tests/data/ettin/<model>.npz`` (Git-ignored; ~0.6 GB per model, mostly the
2048-token logits). Each file holds, per case, ``<case>/input_ids``, ``<case>/attention_mask``
and ``<case>/logits``; decoder files also hold HF greedy generations
(``generate/<i>/prompt_ids`` and ``generate/<i>/output_ids``), and ``meta`` (JSON).
"""

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from scripts.bench_common.dispatch import ROOT

from . import cases
from .loading import EttinTokenizer, read_json, snapshot_path, validate_config

DEFAULT_OUT = ROOT / "tests/data/ettin"


def reference_path(name, out=DEFAULT_OUT):
    return Path(out) / f"{Path(name).name}.npz"


def make_reference(name, out=DEFAULT_OUT, attn_implementation="eager"):
    import torch
    import transformers
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoModelForMaskedLM

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    snapshot, pinned = snapshot_path(name)
    config = read_json(snapshot / "config.json")
    arch = validate_config(config)
    loader = AutoModelForMaskedLM if arch == "encoder" else AutoModelForCausalLM
    model = loader.from_pretrained(snapshot, attn_implementation=attn_implementation, dtype=torch.float32).eval()
    tokenizer = EttinTokenizer(snapshot)
    arrays = {}
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for case, (ids, mask) in cases.parity_inputs(tokenizer, arch).items():
            logits = model(input_ids=torch.from_numpy(ids).long(), attention_mask=torch.from_numpy(mask).long()).logits
            arrays[f"{case}/input_ids"] = ids
            arrays[f"{case}/attention_mask"] = mask
            arrays[f"{case}/logits"] = logits.float().numpy()
        if arch == "decoder":
            for n, prompt in enumerate(cases.GENERATE_PROMPTS):
                prompt_ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt)
                ids = torch.tensor([prompt_ids])
                output = model.generate(
                    input_ids=ids,
                    attention_mask=torch.ones_like(ids),
                    do_sample=False,
                    max_new_tokens=cases.GENERATE_NEW_TOKENS,
                    eos_token_id=config["eos_token_id"],
                    pad_token_id=config["pad_token_id"],
                )
                arrays[f"generate/{n}/prompt_ids"] = np.array(prompt_ids, dtype=np.int32)
                arrays[f"generate/{n}/output_ids"] = output[0, len(prompt_ids) :].numpy().astype(np.int32)
    meta = {

"""Measure Axon-MLX parity against the cached HF references (``make_reference.py``).

Runtime code (no torch). The tests assert thresholds on these measurements; run as a script
it writes the measured numbers for every model to ``log/<run-id>/parity.{json,md}``:

    python -m scripts.ettin_axon.parity --model ettin-encoder-17m ettin-decoder-17m --run-id ettin-parity
"""

import argparse
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np

from scripts.bench_common.dispatch import run_directory, write_json

from . import cases
from .generate import generate
from .loading import load_model
from .make_reference import DEFAULT_OUT, reference_path


def load_reference(name, out=DEFAULT_OUT):
    path = reference_path(name, out)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{path} missing; run: python -m scripts.ettin_axon.make_reference --model {name}")
    reference = np.load(path)
    return reference, json.loads(str(reference["meta"]))


def to_numpy(array):
    return np.array(array.astype(mx.float32))


def logits_metrics(out, ref, mask=None):
    """Max abs diff, max abs diff relative to the largest reference logit, and top-1 agreement.

    ``mask`` ([B, S], 1 = real token) restricts the comparison to non-pad positions.
    """
    keep = np.ones(ref.shape[:2], dtype=bool) if mask is None else mask.astype(bool)
    out, ref = out[keep], ref[keep]
    diff = np.abs(out - ref)
    return {
        "positions": int(keep.sum()),
        "max_abs_diff": float(diff.max()),
        "max_rel_diff": float(diff.max() / np.abs(ref).max()),
        "top1_agreement": float((out.argmax(-1) == ref.argmax(-1)).mean()),
    }


def forward_logits(model, ids, mask):
    if model.arch == "encoder":
        logits, _ = model(ids, mask)
    else:
        logits, _ = model.forward(ids, mask)
    return to_numpy(logits)


def case_parity(model, reference):
    """Full-forward logits for each reference case vs HF."""
    results = {}
    for case in (*cases.LENGTHS, "padded"):
        ids, mask = reference[f"{case}/input_ids"], reference[f"{case}/attention_mask"]
        results[case] = logits_metrics(forward_logits(model, ids, mask), reference[f"{case}/logits"], mask)
    return results


def padding_invariance(model, reference):
    """Each row of the right-padded batch vs the same sequence run alone (non-pad positions)."""
    ids, mask = reference["padded/input_ids"], reference["padded/attention_mask"]
    batch = forward_logits(model, ids, mask)
    rows = []
    for row in range(ids.shape[0]):
        length = int(mask[row].sum())
        alone = forward_logits(model, ids[row : row + 1, :length], None)
        rows.append({"length": length, **logits_metrics(batch[row : row + 1, :length], alone)})
    return rows


def window_edge_positions(length, window):
    """Positions whose sliding window touches a sequence edge or just stops doing so."""
    candidates = [0, 1, window - 1, window, window + 1, 2 * window - 1, 2 * window, 2 * window + 1]
    candidates += [length - 1 - p for p in candidates]
    return sorted({p for p in candidates if 0 <= p < length})


def boundary_parity(model, reference, window):
    """Parity on window-edge positions of the long (> 4x window) case."""
    ids, mask = reference["long/input_ids"], reference["long/attention_mask"]
    if ids.shape[1] <= 4 * window:
        raise ValueError(f"long case has {ids.shape[1]} tokens; need more than 4 x window ({window})")
    positions = window_edge_positions(ids.shape[1], window)
    out = forward_logits(model, ids, mask)[:, positions]
    return {"window": window, "positions": positions, **logits_metrics(out, reference["long/logits"][:, positions])}


def kv_cache_consistency(model, ids, prefill):
    """Prefill ``ids[:prefill]``, then decode the rest one token per step; compare every step
    with one full forward over the same tokens."""
    full, _ = model.forward(ids)
    full = to_numpy(full)
    logits, cache = model.forward(ids[:, :prefill], use_cache=True)
    steps = [to_numpy(logits)]
    for t in range(prefill, ids.shape[1]):
        logits, cache = model.forward(ids[:, t : t + 1], cache=cache, use_cache=True)
        steps.append(to_numpy(logits))
    incremental = np.concatenate(steps, axis=1)
    per_step = np.abs(incremental[0, prefill:] - full[0, prefill:]).max(axis=-1)
    return {
        "prefill": prefill,
        "decode_steps": int(ids.shape[1] - prefill),
        "prefill_max_abs_diff": float(np.abs(incremental[0, :prefill] - full[0, :prefill]).max()),
        "decode_max_abs_diff": float(per_step.max()),
        "worst_step_position": int(prefill + per_step.argmax()),
        "top1_agreement": float((incremental.argmax(-1) == full.argmax(-1)).mean()),
    }


def greedy_match(model, reference):
    """Greedy generation vs HF ``generate(do_sample=False)`` for each reference prompt."""
    results = []
    n = 0
    while f"generate/{n}/prompt_ids" in reference.files:
        prompt = reference[f"generate/{n}/prompt_ids"].tolist()
        expected = reference[f"generate/{n}/output_ids"].tolist()
        got, _ = generate(model, prompt, cases.GENERATE_NEW_TOKENS)
        mismatch = next((i for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(got, expected)) if a != b), None)
        if mismatch is None and len(got) != len(expected):
            mismatch = min(len(got), len(expected))
        results.append({"prompt_tokens": len(prompt), "hf_tokens": len(expected), "axon_tokens": len(got), "exact": got == expected, "first_mismatch": mismatch})
        n += 1
    return results


def measure(name, variant="fused", ref_dir=DEFAULT_OUT, bf16=True):
    """All parity measurements for one model."""
    reference, meta = load_reference(name, ref_dir)
    record = {"model": name, "reference": meta, "variant": variant}
    model = load_model(name, variant=variant)
    record["fast_ops"] = model.info["fast_ops"]
    window = model.config.get("local_attention", 128) // 2
    start = time.perf_counter()

import argparse
import json

    path = reference_path(name, out)

    reference = np.load(path)

def to_numpy(array):
    return np.array(array.astype(mx.float32))


def logits_metrics(out, ref, mask=None):
    """Max abs diff, max abs diff relative to the largest reference logit, and top-1 agreement.

    ``mask`` ([B, S], 1 = real token) restricts the comparison to non-pad positions.
    """
    keep = np.ones(ref.shape[:2], dtype=bool) if mask is None else mask.astype(bool)
    out, ref = out[keep], ref[keep]
    diff = np.abs(out - ref)
    return {
        "positions": int(keep.sum()),
        "max_abs_diff": float(diff.max()),
        "max_rel_diff": float(diff.max() / np.abs(ref).max()),
        "top1_agreement": float((out.argmax(-1) == ref.argmax(-1)).mean()),
    }


def forward_logits(model, ids, mask):
    if model.arch == "encoder":
        logits, _ = model(ids, mask)
    else:
        logits, _ = model.forward(ids, mask)
    return to_numpy(logits)


def case_parity(model, reference):
    """Full-forward logits for each reference case vs HF."""
    results = {}
    for case in (*cases.LENGTHS, "padded"):
        ids, mask = reference[f"{case}/input_ids"], reference[f"{case}/attention_mask"]
        results[case] = logits_metrics(forward_logits(model, ids, mask), reference[f"{case}/logits"], mask)
    return results


def padding_invariance(model, reference):
    """Each row of the right-padded batch vs the same sequence run alone (non-pad positions)."""
    ids, mask = reference["padded/input_ids"], reference["padded/attention_mask"]
    batch = forward_logits(model, ids, mask)
    rows = []
    for row in range(ids.shape[0]):
        length = int(mask[row].sum())
        alone = forward_logits(model, ids[row : row + 1, :length], None)
        rows.append({"length": length, **logits_metrics(batch[row : row + 1, :length], alone)})
    return rows


def window_edge_positions(length, window):
    """Positions whose sliding window touches a sequence edge or just stops doing so."""
    candidates = [0, 1, window - 1, window, window + 1, 2 * window - 1, 2 * window, 2 * window + 1]
    candidates += [length - 1 - p for p in candidates]
    return sorted({p for p in candidates if 0 <= p < length})


def boundary_parity(model, reference, window):
    """Parity on window-edge positions of the long (> 4x window) case."""
    ids, mask = reference["long/input_ids"], reference["long/attention_mask"]
    if ids.shape[1] <= 4 * window:
        raise ValueError(f"long case has {ids.shape[1]} tokens; need more than 4 x window ({window})")
    positions = window_edge_positions(ids.shape[1], window)
    out = forward_logits(model, ids, mask)[:, positions]
    return {"window": window, "positions": positions, **logits_metrics(out, reference["long/logits"][:, positions])}

    """Prefill ``ids[:prefill]``, then decode the rest one token per step; compare every step
    with one full forward over the same tokens."""
    full, _ = model.forward(ids)

    steps = [to_numpy(logits)]
    for t in range(prefill, ids.shape[1]):
        logits, cache = model.forward(ids[:, t : t + 1], cache=cache, use_cache=True)
        steps.append(to_numpy(logits))
    incremental = np.concatenate(steps, axis=1)
    per_step = np.abs(incremental[0, prefill:] - full[0, prefill:]).max(axis=-1)
    return {
        "prefill": prefill,
        "decode_steps": int(ids.shape[1] - prefill),
        "prefill_max_abs_diff": float(np.abs(incremental[0, :prefill] - full[0, :prefill]).max()),
        "decode_max_abs_diff": float(per_step.max()),
        "worst_step_position": int(prefill + per_step.argmax()),

        results.append({"prompt_tokens": len(prompt), "hf_tokens": len(expected), "axon_tokens": len(got), "exact": got == expected, "first_mismatch": mismatch})
        n += 1

"""Measure Axon-MLX parity against the cached HF references (``make_reference.py``).

Runtime code (no torch). The tests assert thresholds on these measurements; run as a script
it writes the measured numbers for every model to ``log/<run-id>/parity.{json,md}``:

    python -m scripts.ettin_axon.parity --model ettin-encoder-17m ettin-decoder-17m --run-id ettin-parity
"""

import argparse
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np

from scripts.bench_common.dispatch import run_directory, write_json

from . import cases
from .generate import generate
from .loading import load_model
from .make_reference import DEFAULT_OUT, reference_path


def load_reference(name, out=DEFAULT_OUT):
    path = reference_path(name, out)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{path} missing; run: python -m scripts.ettin_axon.make_reference --model {name}")
    reference = np.load(path)
    return reference, json.loads(str(reference["meta"]))


def to_numpy(array):
    return np.array(array.astype(mx.float32))


def logits_metrics(out, ref, mask=None):
    """Max abs diff, max abs diff relative to the largest reference logit, and top-1 agreement.

    ``mask`` ([B, S], 1 = real token) restricts the comparison to non-pad positions.
    """
    keep = np.ones(ref.shape[:2], dtype=bool) if mask is None else mask.astype(bool)
    out, ref = out[keep], ref[keep]
    diff = np.abs(out - ref)
    return {
        "positions": int(keep.sum()),
        "max_abs_diff": float(diff.max()),
        "max_rel_diff": float(diff.max() / np.abs(ref).max()),
        "top1_agreement": float((out.argmax(-1) == ref.argmax(-1)).mean()),
    }


def forward_logits(model, ids, mask):
    if model.arch == "encoder":
        logits, _ = model(ids, mask)
    else:
        logits, _ = model.forward(ids, mask)
    return to_numpy(logits)


def case_parity(model, reference):
    """Full-forward logits for each reference case vs HF."""
    results = {}
    for case in (*cases.LENGTHS, "padded"):
        ids, mask = reference[f"{case}/input_ids"], reference[f"{case}/attention_mask"]
        results[case] = logits_metrics(forward_logits(model, ids, mask), reference[f"{case}/logits"], mask)
    return results


def padding_invariance(model, reference):
    """Each row of the right-padded batch vs the same sequence run alone (non-pad positions)."""
    ids, mask = reference["padded/input_ids"], reference["padded/attention_mask"]
    batch = forward_logits(model, ids, mask)
    rows = []
    for row in range(ids.shape[0]):
        length = int(mask[row].sum())
        alone = forward_logits(model, ids[row : row + 1, :length], None)
        rows.append({"length": length, **logits_metrics(batch[row : row + 1, :length], alone)})
    return rows


def window_edge_positions(length, window):
    """Positions whose sliding window touches a sequence edge or just stops doing so."""
    candidates = [0, 1, window - 1, window, window + 1, 2 * window - 1, 2 * window, 2 * window + 1]
    candidates += [length - 1 - p for p in candidates]
    return sorted({p for p in candidates if 0 <= p < length})


def boundary_parity(model, reference, window):
    """Parity on window-edge positions of the long (> 4x window) case."""
    ids, mask = reference["long/input_ids"], reference["long/attention_mask"]
    if ids.shape[1] <= 4 * window:
        raise ValueError(f"long case has {ids.shape[1]} tokens; need more than 4 x window ({window})")
    positions = window_edge_positions(ids.shape[1], window)
    out = forward_logits(model, ids, mask)[:, positions]
    return {"window": window, "positions": positions, **logits_metrics(out, reference["long/logits"][:, positions])}


def kv_cache_consistency(model, ids, prefill):
    """Prefill ``ids[:prefill]``, then decode the rest one token per step; compare every step
    with one full forward over the same tokens."""
    full, _ = model.forward(ids)
    full = to_numpy(full)
    logits, cache = model.forward(ids[:, :prefill], use_cache=True)
    steps = [to_numpy(logits)]
    for t in range(prefill, ids.shape[1]):
        logits, cache = model.forward(ids[:, t : t + 1], cache=cache, use_cache=True)
        steps.append(to_numpy(logits))
    incremental = np.concatenate(steps, axis=1)
    per_step = np.abs(incremental[0, prefill:] - full[0, prefill:]).max(axis=-1)
    return {
        "prefill": prefill,
        "decode_steps": int(ids.shape[1] - prefill),
        "prefill_max_abs_diff": float(np.abs(incremental[0, :prefill] - full[0, :prefill]).max()),
        "decode_max_abs_diff": float(per_step.max()),
        "worst_step_position": int(prefill + per_step.argmax()),
        "top1_agreement": float((incremental.argmax(-1) == full.argmax(-1)).mean()),
    }


def greedy_match(model, reference):
    """Greedy generation vs HF ``generate(do_sample=False)`` for each reference prompt."""
    results = []
    n = 0
    while f"generate/{n}/prompt_ids" in reference.files:
        prompt = reference[f"generate/{n}/prompt_ids"].tolist()
        expected = reference[f"generate/{n}/output_ids"].tolist()
        got, _ = generate(model, prompt, cases.GENERATE_NEW_TOKENS)
        mismatch = next((i for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(got, expected)) if a != b), None)
        if mismatch is None and len(got) != len(expected):
            mismatch = min(len(got), len(expected))
        results.append({"prompt_tokens": len(prompt), "hf_tokens": len(expected), "axon_tokens": len(got), "exact": got == expected, "first_mismatch": mismatch})
        n += 1
    return results


def measure(name, variant="fused", ref_dir=DEFAULT_OUT, bf16=True):
    """All parity measurements for one model."""
    reference, meta = load_reference(name, ref_dir)
    record = {"model": name, "reference": meta, "variant": variant}
    model = load_model(name, variant=variant)
    record["fast_ops"] = model.info["fast_ops"]
    window = model.config.get("local_attention", 128) // 2
    start = time.perf_counter()
    record["fp32"] = case_parity(model, reference)
    record["padding_invariance"] = padding_invariance(model, reference)
    record["boundary"] = boundary_parity(model, reference, window)
    if model.arch == "decoder":
        ids = mx.array(reference["medium/input_ids"])
        record["kv_cache"] = kv_cache_consistency(model, ids, prefill=40)
        record["greedy"] = greedy_match(model, reference)
    if bf16:
        del model
        model = load_model(name, variant=variant, dtype="bfloat16")
        record["bf16"] = case_parity(model, reference)
    record["seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - start
    return record


def markdown(records):
    lines = [
        "| model | case | positions | max abs diff | max rel diff | top-1 |",
        "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|",
    ]
    for record in records:
        for dtype in ("fp32", "bf16"):
            for case, m in record.get(dtype, {}).items():
                lines.append(
                    f"| {record['model']} | {dtype} {case} | {m['positions']} | {m['max_abs_diff']:.2e} | "
                    f"{m['max_rel_diff']:.2e} | {m['top1_agreement'] * 100:.2f}% |"
                )
        b = record["boundary"]
        lines.append(
            f"| {record['model']} | fp32 window edges ({len(b['positions'])} pos) | {b['positions_count'] if 'positions_count' in b else len(b['positions'])} | "
            f"{b['max_abs_diff']:.2e} | {b['max_rel_diff']:.2e} | {b['top1_agreement'] * 100:.2f}% |"
        )
        pad = max(r["max_abs_diff"] for r in record["padding_invariance"])
        lines.append(f"| {record['model']} | padding invariance (batch row vs alone) | | {pad:.2e} | | |")
        if "kv_cache" in record:
            kv = record["kv_cache"]
            lines.append(
                f"| {record['model']} | KV cache: prefill {kv['prefill']} + {kv['decode_steps']} decode steps vs full | | "
                f"{kv['decode_max_abs_diff']:.2e} | | {kv['top1_agreement'] * 100:.2f}% |"
            )
            exact = sum(g["exact"] for g in record["greedy"])
            lines.append(f"| {record['model']} | greedy vs HF generate | {exact}/{len(record['greedy'])} prompts token-exact | | | |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--model", nargs="+", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--variant", default="fused")
    parser.add_argument("--run-id", required=True, help="writes log/<run-id>/parity.{json,md}")
    parser.add_argument("--no-bf16", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    run_dir = run_directory(args.run_id)
    records = []
    for name in args.model:
        records.append(measure(name, args.variant, bf16=not args.no_bf16))
        write_json(run_dir / "parity.json", records)
        print(f"{name}: done in {records[-1]['seconds']:.1f}s")
    (Path(run_dir) / "parity.md").write_text(markdown(records))
    print((Path(run_dir) / "parity.md").read_text())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

questions.question: New evidence on RoPE (you earlier chose 'no synapse changes'). The 2048-token logit errors come from the RoPE builtin computing inv_freq as exp(-log θ·2i/d), while HF uses 1/θ^(2i/d). Swapping in HF's exact cos/sin tables proves it: decoder-17m goes 1.15e-3 → 9e-5 and encoder-32m 4.05e-3 → 1.0e-3. With the pow form computed in MLX (what a builtin fix produces), decoder-17m reaches 1.4e-4 (passes) and encoder-32m 1.76e-3. Without a fix, decoder-17m long fails the 1e-3 target. How should I handle it?

content.text: `pow`'s result type follows its first argument (a Float here). Using a tensor base instead: `fill inv_shape theta`, which `Tensor.axon` already provides.

a = """      inv_shape <- freq_idx / half

b = """      inv_shape <- freq_idx / half
      return 1.0 / (pow (fill inv_shape theta) inv_shape)"""

content.thinking: The fix improved MLX inverse frequency accuracy to 1.4e-7 relative error and 2048-position sin/cos to 3.1e-5, both notable gains over before. I'll now write a regression test probing multiple thetas and head dims with thresholds tight enough to catch the old formula's failure.

"""Regression: default-RoPE inverse frequencies follow HF's ``1 / theta ** (2i / d)``.

The Positions builtins used to compute ``exp(-log(theta) * 2i / d)``, which differs from HF
by up to ~6.5e-7 relative; the angle error grows with position and reached ~1e-3 in the
2048-token Ettin logits. The thresholds below fail for that formula and pass for ``pow``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

import numpy as np
import pytest
import torch

mx = pytest.importorskip("mlx.core")

from scripts.bench_common.cores import COMMON, generate_mlx_core, load_core_class, rewrite_common_import

PROBE = """\
import Positions (position_ids, rope_base_factors, rope_inv_freq_base)
import Config
import Tensor

THETA <- Config.float @@rope_theta default=10000.0

rope_probe :: TokenIds[B,S] -> Tensor[B,H,S,HD] -> (Tensor[B,1,S,HD], Tensor[B,1,S,HD], Tensor[HD / 2])
rope_probe input_ids q = do
  pos <- position_ids input_ids
  sin, cos <- rope_base_factors pos HD THETA
  inv <- rope_inv_freq_base q THETA
  return sin, cos, inv
"""
LENGTH = 2048


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def probe_class(tmp_path_factory):
    directory = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("rope_probe")
    source = directory / "rope_probe.axon"
    source.write_text(PROBE)
    (directory / "core.py").write_text(rewrite_common_import(generate_mlx_core(source, class_name="RopeProbe")))
    shutil.copy2(COMMON, directory / "_axon_common.py")
    return load_core_class(directory / "core.py", "RopeProbe")


def hf_tables(theta, dim, length):
    inv = 1.0 / (torch.tensor(theta) ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2, dtype=torch.float) / dim))
    freqs = torch.arange(length, dtype=torch.float)[:, None] * inv[None]
    emb = torch.cat([freqs, freqs], dim=-1)
    return inv.numpy(), emb.sin().numpy(), emb.cos().numpy()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dim", [64, 128])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("theta", [10000.0, 160000.0, 1000000.0])
def test_rope_tables_match_hf_pow_formula(probe_class, theta, dim):
    core = probe_class({}, config={"rope_theta": theta})
    sin, cos, inv = core._def_rope_probe(mx.zeros((1, LENGTH), dtype=mx.int64), mx.zeros((1, 1, 1, dim)))
    hf_inv, hf_sin, hf_cos = hf_tables(theta, dim, LENGTH)
    inv_rel = np.max(np.abs(np.array(inv) - hf_inv) / hf_inv)
    table = max(np.abs(np.array(sin)[0, 0] - hf_sin).max(), np.abs(np.array(cos)[0, 0] - hf_cos).max())
    assert inv_rel < 3e-7, inv_rel
    assert table < 6e-5, table

"""Regression: default-RoPE inverse frequencies follow HF's ``1 / theta ** (2i / d)``.

The Positions builtins used to compute ``exp(-log(theta) * 2i / d)``, which differs from HF
by up to ~6.5e-7 relative; the angle error grows with position and reached ~1e-3 in the
2048-token Ettin logits. The thresholds below fail for that formula and pass for ``pow``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

import numpy as np
import pytest
import torch

mx = pytest.importorskip("mlx.core")

from scripts.bench_common.cores import COMMON, generate_mlx_core, load_core_class, rewrite_common_import

PROBE = """\
import Positions (position_ids, rope_base_factors, rope_inv_freq_base)
import Config
import Tensor

THETA <- Config.float @@rope_theta default=10000.0

rope_probe :: TokenIds[B,S] -> Tensor[B,H,S,HD] -> (Tensor[B,1,S,HD], Tensor[B,1,S,HD], Tensor[HD / 2])
rope_probe input_ids q = do
  pos <- position_ids input_ids
  sin, cos <- rope_base_factors pos HD THETA
  inv <- rope_inv_freq_base q THETA
  return sin, cos, inv
"""
LENGTH = 2048


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def probe_class(tmp_path_factory):
    directory = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("rope_probe")
    source = directory / "rope_probe.axon"
    source.write_text(PROBE)
    (directory / "core.py").write_text(rewrite_common_import(generate_mlx_core(source, class_name="RopeProbe")))
    shutil.copy2(COMMON, directory / "_axon_common.py")
    return load_core_class(directory / "core.py", "RopeProbe")


def hf_tables(theta, dim, length):
    inv = 1.0 / (torch.tensor(theta) ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2, dtype=torch.float) / dim))
    freqs = torch.arange(length, dtype=torch.float)[:, None] * inv[None]
    emb = torch.cat([freqs, freqs], dim=-1)
    return inv.numpy(), emb.sin().numpy(), emb.cos().numpy()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dim", [64, 128])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("theta", [10000.0, 160000.0, 1000000.0])
def test_rope_tables_match_hf_pow_formula(probe_class, theta, dim):
    core = probe_class({}, config={"rope_theta": theta})
    sin, cos, inv = core._def_rope_probe(mx.zeros((1, LENGTH), dtype=mx.int64), mx.zeros((1, 1, 1, dim)))
    hf_inv, hf_sin, hf_cos = hf_tables(theta, dim, LENGTH)
    inv_rel = np.max(np.abs(np.array(inv) - hf_inv) / hf_inv)
    table = max(np.abs(np.array(sin)[0, 0] - hf_sin).max(), np.abs(np.array(cos)[0, 0] - hf_cos).max())
    assert inv_rel < 3e-7, inv_rel
    assert table < 6e-5, table

def run_axon_materialize_workflow(
    *,
    axon_path: Path,
    checkpoints: list[str] | None = None,
    models_root: Path = Path("models"),
) -> list[Path]:
    resolved_axon = axon_path.resolve()
    resolved_models_root = models_root.resolve()
    if not resolved_axon.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Axon file not found: {resolved_axon}")

    parsed = parse_axon_program_from_path(resolved_axon)
    declared = checkpoint_pragma_entries(parsed.pragmas)
    requested = list(checkpoints or declared)
    if not requested:
        raise ValueError(f"No CHECKPOINTS pragma entries found in {resolved_axon}")

    grouped: list[tuple[Any, list[str]]] = []
    for checkpoint in requested:
        context = load_materialize_context(checkpoint=checkpoint, models_root=resolved_models_root)
        materialized = materialize_axon_file(parsed, context=context)
        for group_ast, group_checkpoints in grouped:
            if ast_equal(group_ast, materialized):
                group_checkpoints.append(checkpoint)
                break
        else:
            grouped.append((materialized, [checkpoint]))

    written: list[Path] = []
    expected: set[Path] = set()
    stale_candidates: set[Path] = set()
    for body_ast, body_checkpoints in grouped:
        out_name = f"{group_output_name(body_checkpoints)}.axon"
        out_path = resolved_axon.parent / out_name
        rendered = render_axon_file(_replace_checkpoints(body_ast, body_checkpoints))
        _atomic_write_text(out_path, rendered)
        expected.add(out_path.resolve())
        written.append(out_path)
        for checkpoint in body_checkpoints:
            stale_candidates.add(
                (resolved_axon.parent / f"{checkpoint.split('/')[-1]}.axon").resolve()
            )
            stale_candidates.add(
                (resolved_axon.parent / f"{normalize_checkpoint_name(checkpoint)}.axon").resolve()
            )

    for stale_path in stale_candidates:
        if stale_path not in expected and stale_path.exists():
            stale_path.unlink()

    return written


__all__ = ["run_axon_materialize_workflow"]

import sys, numpy as np, torch, mlx.core as mx
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from scripts.bench_common.cores import load_core_class
from scripts.ettin_axon import loading
from scripts.ettin_axon.parity import load_reference, logits_metrics, to_numpy
snap = sys.argv[1]; core_file = sys.argv[2]; refname = sys.argv[3]
ref, _ = load_reference(refname)
cfg = loading.read_json(snap + "/config.json")
state = loading.check_state(loading.load_state(snap)[0], cfg, "encoder")
cls = load_core_class(core_file, "C")
d = cfg["hidden_size"] // cfg["num_attention_heads"]
for case in ("medium", "long"):
    ids = ref[f"{case}/input_ids"]; L = ids.shape[1]
    tabs = {}
    for th in (cfg["global_rope_theta"], cfg["local_rope_theta"]):
        inv = 1.0 / (torch.tensor(th) ** (torch.arange(0, d, 2, dtype=torch.float) / d))
        emb = torch.cat([torch.arange(L, dtype=torch.float)[None, :, None] * inv] * 2, -1)
        tabs[th] = (mx.array(emb.sin().numpy())[:, None], mx.array(emb.cos().numpy())[:, None], float(np.sin(inv[1].item())))
    def apply(self, x, sin, cos, traditional=False, use_hf=True):
        if use_hf:
            probe = float(np.array(sin[0, 0, 1, 1]))
            th = min(tabs, key=lambda t: abs(tabs[t][2] - probe))
            sin, cos = tabs[th][0], tabs[th][1]
        h = x.shape[-1] // 2
        return x * cos + mx.concatenate([-x[..., h:], x[..., :h]], -1) * sin
    for label, use_hf in (("builtin tables", False), ("HF torch tables", True)):
        cls._mlx_rope_apply = lambda self, x, s, c, traditional=False, _u=use_hf: apply(self, x, s, c, use_hf=_u)
        core = cls.from_state_dict(dict(state), model_config=cfg)
        out = to_numpy(core._def_modernbert(mx.array(ids), None)[0])
        m = logits_metrics(out, ref[f"{case}/logits"])
        print(f"ModernBERT-base {case} {label:16s} max_abs {m['max_abs_diff']:.3e} top1 {m['top1_agreement']:.4f}  (HF spread {float(ref[f'{case}/hf_spread']):.2e})")
EOF

import sys, numpy as np, torch, mlx.core as mx
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from scripts.bench_common.cores import load_core_class
from scripts.ettin_axon import loading
from scripts.ettin_axon.parity import load_reference, logits_metrics, to_numpy
snap = sys.argv[1]; core_file = sys.argv[2]; refname = sys.argv[3]
ref, _ = load_reference(refname)
cfg = loading.read_json(snap + "/config.json")
state = loading.check_state(loading.load_state(snap)[0], cfg, "encoder")
cls = load_core_class(core_file, "C")
d = cfg["hidden_size"] // cfg["num_attention_heads"]
for case in ("medium", "long"):
    ids = ref[f"{case}/input_ids"]; L = ids.shape[1]
    tabs = {}
    for th in (cfg["global_rope_theta"], cfg["local_rope_theta"]):
        inv = 1.0 / (torch.tensor(th) ** (torch.arange(0, d, 2, dtype=torch.float) / d))
        emb = torch.cat([torch.arange(L, dtype=torch.float)[None, :, None] * inv] * 2, -1)
        tabs[th] = (mx.array(emb.sin().numpy())[:, None], mx.array(emb.cos().numpy())[:, None], float(np.sin(inv[1].item())))
    def apply(self, x, sin, cos, traditional=False, use_hf=True):
        if use_hf:
            probe = float(np.array(sin[0, 0, 1, 1]))
            th = min(tabs, key=lambda t: abs(tabs[t][2] - probe))
            sin, cos = tabs[th][0], tabs[th][1]
        h = x.shape[-1] // 2
        return x * cos + mx.concatenate([-x[..., h:], x[..., :h]], -1) * sin
    for label, use_hf in (("builtin tables", False), ("HF torch tables", True)):
        cls._mlx_rope_apply = lambda self, x, s, c, traditional=False, _u=use_hf: apply(self, x, s, c, use_hf=_u)
        core = cls.from_state_dict(dict(state), model_config=cfg)
        out = to_numpy(core._def_modernbert(mx.array(ids), None)[0])
        m = logits_metrics(out, ref[f"{case}/logits"])
        print(f"ModernBERT-base {case} {label:16s} max_abs {m['max_abs_diff']:.3e} top1 {m['top1_agreement']:.4f}  (HF spread {float(ref[f'{case}/hf_spread']):.2e})")
EOF
.venv/bin/python $S/mb_probe.py $S/models_root/answerdotai/ModernBERT-base $S/gen/enc_rope.py ModernBERT-base 2>&1 | grep -v Warn

content.text: Host package committed. Now performance: decode at about 123 tok/s on a 32m model is far too slow. Profiling one decode step to split Python overhead from GPU time.

input.command:
export HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 && .venv/bin/python - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | grep -v Warn | head -60
import time, cProfile, pstats, io, mlx.core as mx
from scripts.ettin_axon.loading import load_model
m = load_model("ettin-decoder-32m")
ids = mx.array([m.tokenizer.encode("The capital of France is")])
logits, cache = m.forward(ids, use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1)
tok = mx.argmax(logits[:, -1], -1)
mx.eval(tok)
def step(tok, cache):
    logits, cache = m.forward(tok[:, None], cache=cache, use_cache=True)
    tok = mx.argmax(logits[:, -1], -1)
    return tok, cache
for _ in range(10): tok, cache = step(tok, cache); mx.eval(tok)
N = 50
t = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(N): tok, cache = step(tok, cache); mx.eval(tok)
dt = (time.perf_counter() - t) / N
# graph-build time only (no eval)
t = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(N):
    logits, c2 = m.forward(tok[:, None], cache=None, use_cache=False)
build = (time.perf_counter() - t) / N
print(f"step {dt*1000:.2f} ms ({1/dt:.0f} tok/s); python graph build only (no cache, no eval) {build*1000:.2f} ms")
pr = cProfile.Profile(); pr.enable()
for _ in range(20): tok, cache = step(tok, cache); mx.eval(tok)
pr.disable()
s = io.StringIO(); pstats.Stats(pr, stream=s).sort_stats("tottime").print_stats(25); print(s.getvalue()[:6000])
EOF

"""Regression: codegen2-mlx linear honors a runtime (config-driven) bias flag.

The emitter used to look the bias up whenever the flag was not the literal ``false``, so a
false config flag still added a bias present in the state, and an absent bias was re-resolved
(a scan over all state keys) on every call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

import numpy as np
import pytest

from scripts.bench_common.cores import COMMON, generate_mlx_core, load_core_class, rewrite_common_import

mx = pytest.importorskip("mlx.core")

PROBE = """\
import Config
import NN

USE_BIAS <- Config.bool @@use_bias default=false

bias_probe :: Tensor[B,S,D] -> Tensor[B,S,E]
bias_probe x = NN.linear@proj x dim=3 bias=USE_BIAS
"""


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def probe_class(tmp_path_factory):
    directory = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("bias_probe")

toolUseResult.originalFile:
"""Prefill/decode loop for the Ettin decoders: greedy decoding and temperature/top-p sampling.

One full-sequence pass fills the KV cache (keeping only the last position's logits), then
each step feeds one token. Sliding-window layers see the whole cache and mask it to the
window, so cached keys outside the window are excluded exactly as in a full forward.
"""

import time

import mlx.core as mx


def sample_next(logits, *, temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, key=None):
    """Next token id from ``[B, V]`` logits: argmax when ``temperature == 0``.

    Top-p keeps the smallest set of tokens, by descending probability, whose total
    probability reaches ``top_p`` (always at least one token), as HF's TopPLogitsWarper does.
    """
    if temperature <= 0:
        return mx.argmax(logits, axis=-1)
    logits = logits.astype(mx.float32) / temperature
    if top_p < 1.0:
        order = mx.argsort(-logits, axis=-1)
        sorted_logits = mx.take_along_axis(logits, order, axis=-1)
        probs = mx.softmax(sorted_logits, axis=-1)
        before = mx.cumsum(probs, axis=-1) - probs
        sorted_logits = mx.where(before < top_p, sorted_logits, -mx.inf)
        choice = mx.random.categorical(sorted_logits, axis=-1, key=key)
        return mx.take_along_axis(order, choice[..., None], axis=-1)[..., 0]
    return mx.random.categorical(logits, axis=-1, key=key)


def generate(model, prompt_ids, max_new_tokens=64, *, temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, seed=None, eos_token_id=None, stop_at_eos=True):
    """Generate up to ``max_new_tokens`` ids after ``prompt_ids`` (one sequence).

    Returns ``(new_ids, timings)``; ``new_ids`` ends with the EOS id when generation stopped
    there, as HF ``generate`` output does. Every step is synchronous, so the timings are
    wall-clock times of finished work.
    """
    if eos_token_id is None:
        eos_token_id = model.config.get("eos_token_id")
    eos = set(eos_token_id if isinstance(eos_token_id, list) else [eos_token_id]) - {None}
    key = mx.random.key(seed) if seed is not None else None
    ids = mx.array([list(prompt_ids)], dtype=mx.int64)

    start = time.perf_counter()
    logits, cache = model.forward(ids, use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1)
    step_key = None
    if key is not None:
        key, step_key = mx.random.split(key)
    token = sample_next(logits[:, -1, :], temperature=temperature, top_p=top_p, key=step_key)
    mx.eval(token)
    prefill_s = time.perf_counter() - start

    new_ids = []
    decode_start = time.perf_counter()
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):
        next_id = int(token.item())
        new_ids.append(next_id)
        if (stop_at_eos and next_id in eos) or step == max_new_tokens - 1:
            break
        logits, cache = model.forward(token[:, None], cache=cache, use_cache=True)
        if key is not None:
            key, step_key = mx.random.split(key)
        token = sample_next(logits[:, -1, :], temperature=temperature, top_p=top_p, key=step_key)
        mx.eval(token)
    decode_s = time.perf_counter() - decode_start
    decode_steps = max(len(new_ids) - 1, 0)
    return new_ids, {
        "prompt_tokens": len(prompt_ids),
        "new_tokens": len(new_ids),
        "prefill_s": prefill_s,
        "decode_s": decode_s,
        "decode_steps": decode_steps,
        "decode_tokens_per_s": decode_steps / decode_s if decode_steps and decode_s > 0 else None,
    }

"""Ettin on Axon-MLX vs HF transformers (FP32, CPU, eager) on the cached references.

Default models: ettin-{encoder,decoder}-{17m,32m}; 68m-1b are opt-in (``-m large``).
The logits tolerance is 1e-3, or HF's own sdpa-vs-eager spread on a case when that is larger
(see scripts/ettin_axon/make_reference.py and wiki/ettin-axon-mlx.md).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np
import pytest

from scripts.ettin_axon import parity
from tests.ettin_support import ALL_MODELS, DECODERS, ENCODERS, ensure_reference, model


@pytest.fixture(scope="module", params=ALL_MODELS)
def name(request):
    return request.param


@pytest.fixture(scope="module", params=ENCODERS)
def encoder_name(request):
    return request.param


@pytest.fixture(scope="module", params=DECODERS)
def decoder_name(request):
    return request.param


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", parity.CASES)
def test_fp32_logits_match_hf(name, case):
    """Tests 1 and 4: encoder MLM and decoder full-forward logits, FP32."""
    m = parity.case_metrics(model(name), ensure_reference(name), case)
    print(f"{name} {case}: {m}")
    assert m["top1_agreement"] == 1.0
    assert m["max_abs_diff"] < m["tolerance"], m


def test_padding_invariance(name):
    """Test 2: each right-padded batch row matches the sequence run alone (non-pad positions)."""
    reference = ensure_reference(name)
    rows = parity.padding_invariance(model(name), reference)
    bound = parity.tolerance(reference, "padded")
    print(f"{name}: {rows}")
    for row in rows:
        assert row["top1_agreement"] == 1.0
        assert row["max_abs_diff"] < bound, row


def test_sliding_window_edges(name):
    """Test 3: parity on window-edge positions of a sequence longer than 4x the window."""
    m = model(name)
    reference = ensure_reference(name)
    window = m.config["local_attention"] // 2
    result = parity.boundary_parity(m, reference, window)
    print(f"{name}: {result}")
    assert reference["long/input_ids"].shape[1] > 4 * window
    assert result["top1_agreement"] == 1.0
    assert result["max_abs_diff"] < parity.tolerance(reference, "long"), result


def test_kv_cache_matches_full_forward(decoder_name):
    """Test 5: prefill + one-token decode steps vs one full forward, past the sliding window."""
    m = model(decoder_name)
    ids = mx.array(ensure_reference(decoder_name)["medium/input_ids"])
    result = parity.kv_cache_consistency(m, ids, prefill=40)
    print(f"{decoder_name}: {result}")
    window = m.config["local_attention"] // 2
    assert ids.shape[1] - result["prefill"] > 2 * window
    assert result["top1_agreement"] == 1.0
    assert result["prefill_max_abs_diff"] < parity.TARGET_MAX_ABS
    assert result["decode_max_abs_diff"] < parity.TARGET_MAX_ABS, result


def test_greedy_generation_matches_hf(decoder_name):
    """Test 6: token-exact greedy generation vs HF generate(do_sample=False), 64 new tokens."""
    results = parity.greedy_match(model(decoder_name), ensure_reference(decoder_name))
    print(f"{decoder_name}: {results}")
    assert len(results) == 3
    assert all(r["exact"] for r in results), results


@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", parity.CASES)
def test_bf16_against_fp32_reference(name, case):
    """Test 7: BF16 vs the FP32 HF reference. The numbers are reported (``-s``); the only bound
    is a sanity floor on top-1 agreement, since BF16 error is model-dependent (HF's own BF16
    differs from its FP32 by >10 on encoder-32m's 2048-token logits)."""
    m = parity.case_metrics(model(name, "bfloat16"), ensure_reference(name), case)
    print(f"{name} bf16 {case}: max_abs={m['max_abs_diff']:.3e} top1={m['top1_agreement']:.4f}")
    assert np.isfinite(m["max_abs_diff"])
    assert m["top1_agreement"] >= 0.9, m


def test_fill_mask_predicts_paris(encoder_name):
    """Test 9: 'The capital of France is <mask>.' has ' Paris' in the top 5."""
    m = model(encoder_name)
    tok = m.tokenizer
    ids = tok.encode(f"The capital of France is {tok.mask_token}.")
    logits, _ = m([ids])
    row = np.array(logits[0, ids.index(tok.mask_token_id)].astype(mx.float32))
    top5 = [tok.decode([int(t)]).strip() for t in np.argsort(-row)[:5]]
    print(f"{encoder_name}: {top5}")
    assert "Paris" in top5

"""The Axon mask builtins' ``window=`` boundary equals HF masking_utils for ModernBERT/Ettin.

HF keeps |i - j| <= sliding_window for the bidirectional encoder mask and
0 <= i - j < sliding_window for the causal decoder mask, with sliding_window =
local_attention // 2. The models pass ``window=local_attention / 2`` to the builtins.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import shutil

import numpy as np
import pytest
import torch
from transformers import ModernBertConfig, ModernBertDecoderConfig
from transformers.masking_utils import (
    create_bidirectional_sliding_window_mask,
    create_sliding_window_causal_mask,
    sdpa_mask,
    sliding_window_causal_mask_function,
)

from scripts.bench_common.cores import COMMON, generate_mlx_core, load_core_class, rewrite_common_import

mx = pytest.importorskip("mlx.core")

PROBE = """\
import Masking (bidirectional_mask_for_input, causal_mask_for_input)
import Config
import Tensor

WINDOW = (Config.int @@local_attention default=128) / 2

mask_probe :: TokenIds[B,Q] -> Tensor[B,K] -> Dim -> (Tensor[B,1,Q,Q], Tensor[B,1,Q,K])
mask_probe ids padding key_len = do
  bidirectional <- bidirectional_mask_for_input ids Q padding_mask=padding window=WINDOW
  causal <- causal_mask_for_input ids key_len padding_mask=padding window=WINDOW
  return bidirectional, causal
"""
LENGTH = 300
LOCAL_ATTENTION = 128


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def probe(tmp_path_factory):
    directory = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("mask_probe")
    source = directory / "mask_probe.axon"
    source.write_text(PROBE)
    (directory / "core.py").write_text(rewrite_common_import(generate_mlx_core(source, class_name="MaskProbe")))
    shutil.copy2(COMMON, directory / "_axon_common.py")
    return load_core_class(directory / "core.py", "MaskProbe")({}, config={"local_attention": LOCAL_ATTENTION})


def padding_mask():
    mask = np.ones((2, LENGTH), dtype=np.int64)
    mask[1, 211:] = 0
    return mask


def test_bidirectional_window_matches_hf(probe):
    mask = padding_mask()
    axon, _ = probe._def_mask_probe(mx.zeros(mask.shape, dtype=mx.int64), mx.array(mask), LENGTH)
    config = ModernBertConfig(local_attention=LOCAL_ATTENTION)
    config._attn_implementation = "eager"
    hf = create_bidirectional_sliding_window_mask(config, torch.zeros(2, LENGTH, 8), torch.from_numpy(mask)) == 0
    assert config.sliding_window == 64
    assert np.array_equal(np.array(axon), hf.numpy())


def test_causal_window_matches_hf(probe):
    mask = padding_mask()
    _, axon = probe._def_mask_probe(mx.zeros(mask.shape, dtype=mx.int64), mx.array(mask), LENGTH)
    config = ModernBertDecoderConfig(local_attention=LOCAL_ATTENTION)
    config._attn_implementation = "eager"
    positions = torch.arange(LENGTH)[None].expand(2, -1)
    hf = create_sliding_window_causal_mask(config, torch.zeros(2, LENGTH, 8), torch.from_numpy(mask), None, positions) == 0
    assert config.sliding_window == 64
    assert np.array_equal(np.array(axon), hf.numpy())


@pytest.mark.parametrize("key_len", [64, 65, 128, 129, 300])
def test_causal_window_with_cache_offset_matches_hf(probe, key_len):
    """One query at position key_len - 1 over a cache of key_len keys (a decode step)."""
    _, axon = probe._def_mask_probe(mx.zeros((1, 1), dtype=mx.int64), mx.ones((1, key_len), dtype=mx.int64), key_len)
    hf = sdpa_mask(
        batch_size=1,
        q_length=1,
        kv_length=key_len,
        q_offset=key_len - 1,
        mask_function=sliding_window_causal_mask_function(LOCAL_ATTENTION // 2),
        allow_is_causal_skip=False,
    )
    assert int(np.array(axon).sum()) == min(key_len, LOCAL_ATTENTION // 2)
    assert np.array_equal(np.array(axon), hf.numpy())

"""Ettin loading: the torch-free checkpoint reader, the strict key check, config validation,
the tokenizer rules, and that the generated core reads exactly the HF parameter names."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import pickle
import zipfile

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np
import pytest
import torch

from scripts.ettin_axon import loading
from scripts.ettin_axon.checkpoint import load_torch_bin
from tests.ettin_support import ensure_cores

SMALL = ("ettin-encoder-17m", "ettin-decoder-17m")


def snapshot(name):
    return loading.snapshot_path(name)[0]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", SMALL)
def test_bin_reader_matches_torch_load(name):
    path = snapshot(name) / "pytorch_model.bin"
    ours = load_torch_bin(path)
    theirs = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    assert set(ours) == set(theirs)
    for key, value in theirs.items():
        assert ours[key].dtype == mx.float32
        assert np.array_equal(np.array(ours[key]), value.numpy()), key


def test_bin_reader_reads_bfloat16(tmp_path):
    tensors = {"w": torch.randn(3, 5).to(torch.bfloat16), "t": torch.randn(4, 6)[:, 1:4].t()}
    torch.save(tensors, tmp_path / "pytorch_model.bin")
    ours = load_torch_bin(tmp_path / "pytorch_model.bin")
    assert ours["w"].dtype == mx.bfloat16
    assert np.array_equal(np.array(ours["w"].astype(mx.float32)), tensors["w"].float().numpy())
    assert np.array_equal(np.array(ours["t"]), tensors["t"].numpy())


def test_bin_reader_refuses_foreign_globals(tmp_path):
    class Evil:
        def __reduce__(self):
            return (print, ("pwned",))

    path = tmp_path / "pytorch_model.bin"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as archive:
        archive.writestr("archive/data.pkl", pickle.dumps({"x": Evil()}, protocol=2))
    with pytest.raises(pickle.UnpicklingError, match="builtins.print"):
        load_torch_bin(path)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", SMALL)
def test_expected_shapes_match_hf_parameters(name):
    from transformers import AutoConfig, AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoModelForMaskedLM

    config = loading.read_json(snapshot(name) / "config.json")
    arch = loading.validate_config(config)
    hf_config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(snapshot(name))
    with torch.device("meta"):
        hf = (AutoModelForMaskedLM if arch == "encoder" else AutoModelForCausalLM).from_config(hf_config)
    hf_shapes = {k: tuple(v.shape) for k, v in hf.state_dict().items() if k != loading.TIED_DECODER_KEY}
    assert loading.expected_shapes(config, arch) == hf_shapes


def test_expected_shapes_honor_bias_flags():
    config = loading.read_json(snapshot("ettin-decoder-17m") / "config.json")
    config.update(attention_bias=True, mlp_bias=True, norm_bias=True, classifier_bias=True, decoder_bias=False)
    shapes = loading.expected_shapes(config, "decoder")
    assert "model.layers.1.attn.q_proj.bias" in shapes
    assert "model.layers.1.mlp.Wi.bias" in shapes
    assert "model.layers.1.attn_norm.bias" in shapes
    assert "lm_head.dense.bias" in shapes
    assert "decoder.bias" not in shapes


def _state_and_config(name):
    config = loading.read_json(snapshot(name) / "config.json")
    state, _ = loading.load_state(snapshot(name))
    return state, config


def test_check_state_drops_tied_decoder_weight():
    state, config = _state_and_config("ettin-encoder-17m")
    assert loading.TIED_DECODER_KEY in state
    checked = loading.check_state(state, config, "encoder")
    assert loading.TIED_DECODER_KEY not in checked
    assert set(checked) == set(loading.expected_shapes(config, "encoder"))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "mutate, message",
    [
        (lambda s: s.pop("model.layers.3.mlp.Wo.weight"), "missing=\\['model.layers.3.mlp.Wo.weight'\\]"),
        (lambda s: s.__setitem__("model.layers.0.attn_norm.weight", mx.ones((256,))), "unexpected=\\['model.layers.0.attn_norm.weight'\\]"),
        (lambda s: s.__setitem__("head.dense.weight", mx.ones((256, 255))), "misshapen=\\['head.dense.weight"),
        (lambda s: s.__setitem__(loading.TIED_DECODER_KEY, mx.ones((7, 256))), "tied decoder.weight"),
    ],
)
def test_check_state_fails_loudly(mutate, message):
    state, config = _state_and_config("ettin-encoder-17m")
    mutate(state)
    with pytest.raises(loading.CheckpointError, match=message):
        loading.check_state(state, config, "encoder")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "change, message",
    [
        ({"hidden_activation": "silu"}, "hidden_activation"),
        ({"rope_scaling": {"rope_type": "linear", "factor": 2.0}}, "rope_scaling"),
        ({"rope_parameters": {"full_attention": {"rope_type": "yarn"}}}, "rope_type"),
        ({"layer_types": ["full_attention"] * 3}, "layer_types length"),
        ({"model_type": "bert"}, "model_type"),
        ({"tie_word_embeddings": False}, None),
    ],
)
def test_validate_config_rejects_unsupported(change, message):
    config = {**loading.read_json(snapshot("ettin-decoder-17m") / "config.json"), **change}
    if message is None:
        state, _ = loading.load_state(snapshot("ettin-decoder-17m"))
        with pytest.raises(loading.CheckpointError, match="tie_word_embeddings"):
            loading.check_state(state, config, "decoder")
        return
    with pytest.raises(loading.CheckpointError, match=message):
        loading.validate_config(config)


class _Recording(dict):
    def __init__(self, data):
        super().__init__(data)
        self.read = set()

    def __getitem__(self, key):
        self.read.add(key)
        return super().__getitem__(key)

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        if key in self:
            self.read.add(key)
        return super().get(key, default)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", SMALL)
def test_core_reads_exactly_the_checkpoint_names(name):
    """The .axon scopes are the HF names: a forward reads every checked key and nothing else."""
    ensure_cores()
    model = loading.load_model(name)
    recording = _Recording(model.core._flat_tensors)
    object.__setattr__(model.core, "_flat_tensors", recording)
    object.__setattr__(model.core, "_param_cache", {})
    ids = model.tokenizer.encode("hello world")
    logits = model([ids])[0] if model.arch == "encoder" else model.forward([ids])[0]
    mx.eval(logits)
    assert recording.read == set(loading.expected_shapes(model.config, model.arch))


def test_stale_cores_are_refused(tmp_path):
    ensure_cores()
    manifest = json.loads((loading.DEFAULT_CORES / "fused/manifest.json").read_text())
    (tmp_path / "fused").mkdir()
    manifest["archs"]["encoder"]["axon_sha256"] = "0" * 64
    (tmp_path / "fused/manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="changed since the cores were built"):
        loading.load_core("encoder", cores_dir=tmp_path)


def test_encoder_tokenizer_matches_hf():
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer

    hf = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(snapshot("ettin-encoder-17m"))
    ours = loading.EttinTokenizer(snapshot("ettin-encoder-17m"))
    for text in ("The capital of France is [MASK].", "  Hello,\tworld!  ", "naïve café — 123"):
        assert ours.encode(text) == hf(text)["input_ids"]
    assert ours.mask_token_id == hf.mask_token_id
    assert ours.pad_token_id == hf.pad_token_id


def test_decoder_tokenizer_prepends_bos():
    """tokenizer_config.json sets add_bos_token (and no EOS); transformers 5.x drops the flag
    and adds no BOS, which the decoders need. We follow the config."""
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer

    hf = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(snapshot("ettin-decoder-17m"))
    ours = loading.EttinTokenizer(snapshot("ettin-decoder-17m"))
    assert ours.flags == {"add_bos_token": True}
    for text in ("The capital of France is", "Once upon a time,"):
        assert ours.encode(text) == [hf.bos_token_id, *hf(text)["input_ids"]]
    assert ours.eos_token_id == hf.eos_token_id


def test_right_padding():
    tok = loading.EttinTokenizer(snapshot("ettin-encoder-17m"))
    ids, mask = tok.pad([[1, 2, 3], [4]])
    assert ids.tolist() == [[1, 2, 3], [4, tok.pad_token_id, tok.pad_token_id]]
    assert mask.tolist() == [[1, 1, 1], [1, 0, 0]]


def test_bin_reader_handles_a_buffer_shared_by_two_tensors(tmp_path):
    base = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.float32)
    torch.save({"a": base[:6].view(2, 3), "b": base[6:]}, tmp_path / "pytorch_model.bin")
    ours = load_torch_bin(tmp_path / "pytorch_model.bin")
    assert np.array_equal(np.array(ours["a"]), np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3))
    assert np.array_equal(np.array(ours["b"]), np.arange(6, 12))
    assert io.BytesIO  # keep io imported for readers of this module's helpers

"""Sampling in scripts/ettin_axon/generate.py, and the ModernBERT-base regression for the
shared encoder axon (run when the checkpoint is in the HF cache)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np
import pytest

from scripts.ettin_axon.generate import generate, sample_next
from tests.ettin_support import ensure_cores, model


def test_temperature_zero_is_argmax():
    logits = mx.array([[0.1, 3.0, -1.0, 2.9], [5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]])
    assert sample_next(logits).tolist() == [1, 0]


def test_top_p_keeps_the_smallest_nucleus():
    # probabilities 0.5, 0.3, 0.2: top_p 0.5 keeps only the first, 0.6 the first two
    logits = mx.log(mx.array([[0.3, 0.5, 0.2]]))
    keys = mx.random.split(mx.random.key(0), 200)
    only_top = {sample_next(logits, temperature=1.0, top_p=0.5, key=k).item() for k in keys}
    top_two = {sample_next(logits, temperature=1.0, top_p=0.6, key=k).item() for k in keys}
    assert only_top == {1}
    assert top_two == {0, 1}


def test_sampling_is_seeded():
    ensure_cores()
    decoder = model("ettin-decoder-17m")
    prompt = decoder.tokenizer.encode("Once upon a time")
    first, _ = generate(decoder, prompt, 16, temperature=0.9, top_p=0.95, seed=3, stop_at_eos=False)
    second, _ = generate(decoder, prompt, 16, temperature=0.9, top_p=0.95, seed=3, stop_at_eos=False)
    greedy, _ = generate(decoder, prompt, 16, stop_at_eos=False)
    assert first == second
    assert len(first) == 16 and len(greedy) == 16


def _modernbert_base():
    try:
        from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download

        return snapshot_download("answerdotai/ModernBERT-base", allow_patterns=["*.json", "*.safetensors"], local_files_only=True)
    except Exception:
        return None


@pytest.mark.skipif(_modernbert_base() is None, reason="answerdotai/ModernBERT-base is not in the HF cache")
def test_modernbert_base_still_matches_hf():
    """generic-modernbert.axon still serves ModernBERT-base (two RoPE thetas, safetensors
    weights through mx.load). It is ill-conditioned at length (HF's own sdpa and eager differ
    by ~3e-3 at 300 tokens), so beyond 8 tokens the bound is relative to the logit scale."""
    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM

    from scripts.ettin_axon.cases import parity_inputs
    from scripts.ettin_axon.loading import load_model
    from scripts.ettin_axon.parity import logits_metrics, to_numpy

    ensure_cores()
    snapshot = _modernbert_base()
    ours = load_model(snapshot)
    assert ours.info["weight_files"] == ["model.safetensors"]
    hf = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained(snapshot, attn_implementation="eager", dtype=torch.float32).eval()
    inputs = parity_inputs(ours.tokenizer, "encoder")
    for case in ("short", "medium", "padded"):
        ids, mask = inputs[case]
        with torch.inference_mode():
            ref = hf(input_ids=torch.from_numpy(ids).long(), attention_mask=torch.from_numpy(mask).long()).logits.numpy()
        m = logits_metrics(to_numpy(ours(ids, mask)[0]), ref, mask)
        print(f"ModernBERT-base {case}: {m}")
        assert m["top1_agreement"] == 1.0
        assert m["max_rel_diff"] < 1e-4, m
        if case == "short":
            assert m["max_abs_diff"] < 1e-3, m
    assert np.isfinite(m["max_abs_diff"])

Tests (default models ettin-{encoder,decoder}-{17m,32m}; 68m-1b behind the new
opt-in 'large' marker, registered in pyproject.toml and skipped unless -m
large selects it):
- test_ettin_parity: FP32 logits vs HF (short/medium/long/padded), padding
  invariance, window-edge positions on a >4x-window sequence, KV cache vs full
  forward, greedy generation vs HF generate, BF16 numbers, fill-mask.
- test_ettin_masks: the mask builtins' window= boundary equals HF
  masking_utils (bidirectional, causal, cache offsets).
- test_ettin_loading: torch-free .bin reader, strict key check, config
  validation, the shape table vs HF modules, the core reads exactly the HF
  names, stale cores, tokenizer rules.
- test_ettin_isolation: a subprocess that loads and runs the cores has no
  torch, transformers or synapse in sys.modules.
- test_ettin_generate: sampling, plus a ModernBERT-base regression check.

generate.py queues the next decode step (mx.async_eval) before reading the
current token, so graph building overlaps GPU work (32m: 264 -> 485 tok/s).
EttinEncoder.embed returns only the last hidden state, so the vocab
projection is never computed.

content.text: Writing `bench.py`: an orchestrator that runs one fresh worker process per model (via `bench_common.dispatch`), plus the worker that times the cells.

input.content:
"""Latency and throughput of Ettin on the Axon-generated MLX cores.

    caffeinate -i python -m scripts.ettin_axon.bench --run-id ettin-bench-<date> [--model ...]

Each model runs in a fresh worker process (``bench_common.dispatch``). Cells:
- encoder forward to the last hidden state (``embed``): batch x sequence, FP32/BF16,
  eager and ``mx.compile``; plus the full MLM forward (logits) at batch 1;
- decoder prefill (one pass that fills the KV cache, last-position logits) and the full
  forward without a cache (eager and ``mx.compile``); decode tokens/s at batch 1.
Protocol per cell: warmup runs, then timed runs, each ending in ``mx.eval`` of the outputs;
median, p10 and p90 of the timed runs; peak memory from ``mx.get_peak_memory`` after a
reset at the start of the cell. Writes ``log/<run-id>/{results.json,table.md}`` with the
machine, MLX, checkpoint revisions, Axon commit and build settings.
"""

import argparse
import gc
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np

from scripts.bench_common.dispatch import read_json, run_directory, run_worker, wait_for_idle, write_json
from scripts.bench_common.provenance import distribution_version, git_state, machine_snapshot

from . import cases, revisions
from .generate import generate
from .loading import core_manifest, load_model

MODULE = "scripts.ettin_axon.bench"
DEFAULT_MODELS = tuple(name for name in revisions.REVISIONS)
DEFAULTS = {
    "encoder_batches": [1, 8],
    "encoder_lengths": [128, 512, 2048, 8192],
    "mlm_lengths": [128, 512, 2048, 8192],
    "prefill_lengths": [128, 512, 2048],
    "decode_prompt": 128,
    "decode_tokens": 128,
    "dtypes": ["float32", "bfloat16"],
    "warmup": 2,
    "repeats": 5,
    "variant": "fused",
}


def summarize(times, peak_bytes, **extra):
    ms = np.array(times) * 1000
    return {
        "median_ms": float(np.median(ms)),
        "p10_ms": float(np.percentile(ms, 10)),
        "p90_ms": float(np.percentile(ms, 90)),
        "runs": len(times),
        "peak_memory_gb": peak_bytes / 1e9,
        **extra,
    }


def timed(run, warmup, repeats):
    """Warm up, reset the peak, then time ``repeats`` runs; ``run`` returns arrays to eval."""
    for _ in range(warmup):
        mx.eval(run())
    mx.clear_cache()
    mx.reset_peak_memory()
    times = []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        mx.eval(run())
        times.append(time.perf_counter() - start)
    return times, mx.get_peak_memory()


def batch_ids(tokenizer, arch, batch, length):
    rows = [cases.sequence(tokenizer, arch, length, seed=100 + row) for row in range(batch)]
    return mx.array(np.array(rows, dtype=np.int64))


def encoder_cells(name, dtype, options):
    cells = []
    for compiled in (False, True):
        model = load_model(name, dtype=dtype, variant=options["variant"], compile=compiled)
        for batch in options["encoder_batches"]:
            for length in options["encoder_lengths"]:
                ids = batch_ids(model.tokenizer, "encoder", batch, length)
                times, peak = timed(lambda: model.embed(ids), options["warmup"], options["repeats"])
                cells.append({"kind": "encoder_embed", "dtype": dtype, "compile": compiled, "batch": batch, "length": length,
                              **summarize(times, peak, tokens_per_s=batch * length / np.median(times))})
                print(json.dumps(cells[-1]), flush=True)
        for length in options["mlm_lengths"]:
            ids = batch_ids(model.tokenizer, "encoder", 1, length)
            times, peak = timed(lambda: model(ids)[0], options["warmup"], options["repeats"])
            cells.append({"kind": "encoder_mlm", "dtype": dtype, "compile": compiled, "batch": 1, "length": length,
                          **summarize(times, peak, tokens_per_s=length / np.median(times))})
            print(json.dumps(cells[-1]), flush=True)
        del model
        gc.collect()
        mx.clear_cache()
    return cells


def decoder_cells(name, dtype, options):
    cells = []
    for compiled in (False, True):
        model = load_model(name, dtype=dtype, variant=options["variant"], compile=compiled)
        for length in options["prefill_lengths"]:
            ids = batch_ids(model.tokenizer, "decoder", 1, length)
            if not compiled:

                def prefill():
                    logits, cache = model.forward(ids, use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1)
                    return [logits, *[t for layer in cache for t in (layer[0], layer[1])]]

                times, peak = timed(prefill, options["warmup"], options["repeats"])
                cells.append({"kind": "decoder_prefill", "dtype": dtype, "compile": False, "batch": 1, "length": length,
                              **summarize(times, peak, tokens_per_s=length / np.median(times))})
                print(json.dumps(cells[-1]), flush=True)
            times, peak = timed(lambda: model.forward(ids, logits_to_keep=1)[0], options["warmup"], options["repeats"])
            cells.append({"kind": "decoder_forward", "dtype": dtype, "compile": compiled, "batch": 1, "length": length,
                          **summarize(times, peak, tokens_per_s=length / np.median(times))})
            print(json.dumps(cells[-1]), flush=True)
        if not compiled:
            prompt = cases.sequence(model.tokenizer, "decoder", options["decode_prompt"], seed=7)
            for _ in range(options["warmup"]):
                generate(model, prompt, options["decode_tokens"], stop_at_eos=False)
            mx.clear_cache()
            mx.reset_peak_memory()
            rates, step_ms = [], []
            for _ in range(options["repeats"]):
                _, t = generate(model, prompt, options["decode_tokens"], stop_at_eos=False)
                rates.append(t["decode_tokens_per_s"])
                step_ms.append(1000 * t["decode_s"] / t["decode_steps"])
            cells.append({"kind": "decoder_decode", "dtype": dtype, "compile": False, "batch": 1, "length": options["decode_prompt"],
                          "new_tokens": options["decode_tokens"], "tokens_per_s_median": float(np.median(rates)),
                          "tokens_per_s_p10": float(np.percentile(rates, 10)), "tokens_per_s_p90": float(np.percentile(rates, 90)),
                          **summarize(np.array(step_ms) / 1000, mx.get_peak_memory())})
            print(json.dumps(cells[-1]), flush=True)
        del model
        gc.collect()
        mx.clear_cache()
    return cells


def worker(name, out, options):
    options = {**DEFAULTS, **json.loads(options)}
    arch = "encoder" if "encoder" in name else "decoder"
    cells = []
    for dtype in options["dtypes"]:
        cells += (encoder_cells if arch == "encoder" else decoder_cells)(name, dtype, options)
    write_json(out, {"model": name, "arch": arch, "repo_id": revisions.repo_id(name), "revision": revisions.revision(name), "cells": cells})


def environment(options):
    manifest = core_manifest(options["variant"])
    return {
        "machine": machine_snapshot(["mlx", "numpy", "tokenizers", "huggingface_hub", "safetensors"]),
        "device": mx.device_info(),
        "mlx": distribution_version("mlx"),
        "axon_git": git_state(),
        "build": {k: manifest[k] for k in ("variant", "optimize", "backend_intrinsics", "git", "builtins_sha256")},
        "fast_ops": {arch: info["fast_ops"] for arch, info in manifest["archs"].items()},
        "revisions": revisions.REVISIONS,
        "options": options,
    }


def _ms(cell):
    return f"{cell['median_ms']:.1f} ({cell['p10_ms']:.1f}-{cell['p90_ms']:.1f})"


def table(results):
    lines = []
    encoders = [r for r in results if r["arch"] == "encoder"]
    decoders = [r for r in results if r["arch"] == "decoder"]
    if encoders:
        lines += ["### Encoder forward to the last hidden state (ms: median (p10-p90); peak GB)", "",
                  "| model | dtype | batch | seq | eager | mx.compile | compile speedup | peak GB (eager) |", "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|"]
        for r in encoders:
            cells = {(c["kind"], c["dtype"], c["compile"], c["batch"], c["length"]): c for c in r["cells"]}
            for (kind, dtype, compiled, batch, length), cell in cells.items():
                if kind != "encoder_embed" or compiled:
                    continue
                comp = cells.get((kind, dtype, True, batch, length))
                speed = f"{cell['median_ms'] / comp['median_ms']:.2f}x" if comp else "-"
                lines.append(f"| {r['model']} | {dtype} | {batch} | {length} | {_ms(cell)} | {_ms(comp) if comp else '-'} | {speed} | {cell['peak_memory_gb']:.2f} |")
        lines += ["", "### Encoder MLM forward with full logits, batch 1 (ms)", "",
                  "| model | dtype | seq | eager | mx.compile | peak GB (eager) |", "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|"]
        for r in encoders:
            cells = {(c["kind"], c["dtype"], c["compile"], c["length"]): c for c in r["cells"]}
            for (kind, dtype, compiled, length), cell in cells.items():
                if kind == "encoder_mlm" and not compiled:
                    comp = cells.get((kind, dtype, True, length))
                    lines.append(f"| {r['model']} | {dtype} | {length} | {_ms(cell)} | {_ms(comp) if comp else '-'} | {cell['peak_memory_gb']:.2f} |")
    if decoders:
        lines += ["", "### Decoder, batch 1 (ms: median (p10-p90))", "",
                  "| model | dtype | prompt | prefill (fills cache) | forward, no cache | forward, mx.compile | peak GB (prefill) |", "|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|"]
        for r in decoders:
            cells = {(c["kind"], c["dtype"], c["compile"], c["length"]): c for c in r["cells"]}
            for (kind, dtype, compiled, length), cell in cells.items():
                if kind != "decoder_prefill":
                    continue
                fwd = cells.get(("decoder_forward", dtype, False, length))
                comp = cells.get(("decoder_forward", dtype, True, length))

median, p10 and p90 of the timed runs; peak memory from ``mx.get_peak_memory`` after a
reset at the start of the cell. Writes ``log/<run-id>/{results.json,table.md}`` with the
machine, MLX, checkpoint revisions, Axon commit and build settings.

import gc
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import mlx.core as mx
import numpy as np

    for _ in range(warmup):
        mx.eval(run())
    mx.clear_cache()
    mx.reset_peak_memory()
    times = []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        mx.eval(run())

    return times, mx.get_peak_memory()

    cells = []

            for length in options["encoder_lengths"]:
                ids = batch_ids(model.tokenizer, "encoder", batch, length)
                times, peak = timed(lambda: model.embed(ids), options["warmup"], options["repeats"])
                cells.append({"kind": "encoder_embed", "dtype": dtype, "compile": compiled, "batch": batch, "length": length,
                              **summarize(times, peak, tokens_per_s=batch * length / np.median(times))})
